text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia is considering cutting imports of sugar, potatoes, cigarettes, margarine, non-alcohol drinks, spirits and beer by introducing import quotas, the director of the Czech-Slovak customs union council Rudolf Besik said.
- A 2.7 billion crown debt shoe producer CEBO Holding Slovakia a.s. (CHS) could be the motive for the assasination of the company's Vice-president Pavol Bezak, Interior Minister Gustav Krajci said.
(Bezak was shot dead on Friday. He is the second CHS top executive killed this year, after an unknown assailant shot dead President Anton Jasik in February.)

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar rejects the idea of the direct election of the President, but added he did not believe that parliament, in its present shape, would vote successfuly on a new candidate in 1998 when the term of Michal Kovac expires.

PRAVDA - Chairman of the Slovak National Party (SNS) Jan Slota said he was convinced the controversial amendment to the penal code, known as the law on protection of the republic, would be approved by parliament on Tuesday.
- Frantisek Gaulieder, a deputy who was recently expelled from the parliament after he left the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), has appealed to the Constitutional Court.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak Ministry of Telecomunications will propose the transformation of state Slovak Telecomunications (ST) into a joint-stock company, though it would remain wholl state-owned.
- The Minstry of Transport will transform state Slovak Railways (ZSR) into a 100-percent state held joint-stock company by the end of the next year.

- Slovakia's annual $1 billion trade deficit with Russia is the only problem between the two countries, Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik said. Slovakia should solve this problem mainly by cooperating with Russia in energy production, the heavy industry sector and oil refining, Hamzik said.
